subject: Private deployment interface catalog + traffic fingerprint review
messages:
From: Maria Garcia <maria.garcia@colossuscloud.com>
To: Soojin Lee <soojin.lee@redwood.com>, SRE <sre@edgewave.com>
Cc: procurement@edgewave.com
Date: 2026-08-12T09:14:00-07:00
Subject: Re: On-prem deployment — interface catalog request

Hi Soojin,

Thanks for the demo last week. EdgeWave is starting internal planning for a private deployment and the infra team asked for two things we couldn't finish on the call: an interface catalog mapping control-plane <> data-plane endpoints and a short "traffic fingerprint" sample showing typical token-level ingress/egress patterns (TCP ports, expected payload size ranges, and common sequence lengths) so their network team can size and QA the firewall/NAT behavior.

Can your team share a concise reference (diagram + a CSV sample of fingerprints) and call out any non-standard egress we use (eg: telemetry, metrics collectors, licensing calls)? We need this to get our security review and procurement timeline moving.

Thanks — Maria
EdgeWave (on behalf of SRE)<attachment: traffic-fingerprint-sample.csv>

From: Soojin Lee <soojin.lee@redwood.com>

Subject: Fwd: On-prem deployment — interface catalog request

Folks — forwarding EdgeWave's ask. Short timeline: they need an interface catalog + a small traffic fingerprint sample for their network/security review. Initial constraints:
- Must show control plane endpoints (registration, control API, cert propagation) vs data plane (inference endpoints, batch ingestion).
- Call out outgoing telemetry (Prometheus pushgateway vs pull?), metrics/health ping intervals, and license-check endpoints (if any).
- Provide a sample CSV with 10–20 rows of representative connections (source role, dest host:port, avg payload bytes, seq len distribution).

Jonas, can you sketch an annotated diagram and a simple CSV? Neha — please flag any compliance notes (data retention/PII egress) we should call out. Kimberly — please check SLA variance language (we may need to mark any call that bypasses private plane as best-effort).

Target: deliver first-pass package to Maria by EOD tomorrow (2026-08-13).

Thanks — Soojin
Soojin Lee

From: Jonas Weber <jonas.weber@redwood.com>
To: Soojin Lee <soojin.lee@redwood.com>, neha.kapoor@redwood.com, kimberly.park@redwood.com
Cc: maria.garcia@colossuscloud.com, sre@edgewave.com
Date: 2026-08-12T15:46:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Fwd: On-prem deployment — interface catalog request

Soojin / team — attaching a simple annotated wiring diagram and a first-pass interface catalog (PDF). Key callouts in the diagram:
- Control plane: control.redwood.internal:443 (TLS, mutual TLS required for cert exchange), cp-registry:8081 (registration + heartbeats), cp-ops:9411 (tracing/ops endpoint; outbound to Redwoods' observability cluster if opted).
- Data plane: dp-runtime nodes accept inference on 127.0.0.1:8080 behind the local sidecar which exposes tenant-facing endpoints on the customer load balancer IP:8443.
- KV-cache sync happens over an internal gRPC channel (dp-kvcache:50051) — this is internal-only and requires no external NAT.
- Telemetry: by default we push metrics to a configured Prometheus pushgateway (outbound 9091) if the customer opts in; otherwise we expose /metrics and expect the customer's Prometheus to scrape.

I've also generated a small traffic fingerprint CSV (attached) with 15 sample rows: expected request sizes for typical completion (short chat 300–800 bytes, long batch 5–15 KB), token sequence length distribution column, and example TLS SNI values. One explicit note: license-check (license.redwood.com:443) is optional and only used for specific enterprise features and remote telemetry. Recommend customers whitelist it only if they enable those features.

I'll iterate on the catalog after Neha's compliance review.

— Jonas
Principal Infra Eng — Private Deploy
<attachment: edgewave_iface_catalog_v1.pdf>
<attachment: traffic-fingerprint-sample.csv>

From: Neha Kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwood.com>
To: Jonas Weber <jonas.weber@redwood.com>, Soojin Lee <soojin.lee@redwood.com>, kimberly.park@redwood.com
Cc: maria.garcia@colossuscloud.com, sre@edgewave.com
Date: 2026-08-13T09:18:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Fwd: On-prem deployment — interface catalog request

Thanks — quick compliance notes for the catalog before we send to procurement/security: 
- Data retention: mark that control-plane logs (registration events, heartbeats) are retained by default for 7 days in the local ops bundle; customers can configure longer retention if required. Call out any fields in logs that may include user identifiers — we only surface opaque tenant_id and request_id; no prompt content is emitted to control-plane logs.
- KV cache: reaffirm that the KV cache channel never leaves the private fabric unless customer explicitly configures cross-region replication. If EdgeWave wants cross-region, we need a separate checklist.
- Egress/Telemetry: Prometheus pushgateway outbound is to a customer-controlled collector if so configured. If customer chooses Redwood's managed observability, then outbound endpoints to telemetry.redwood.com are used — mark that as optional and subject to contractual consent.
- SLA variance: Kimberly, please add a short blurb that any feature requiring outbound license-checks or managed telemetry is excluded from the private deployment SLA unless explicitly added to the contract.

I'll run a short redline and send the updated PDF by noon.

— Neha
Security & Compliance

From: Soojin Lee <soojin.lee@redwood.com>
To: Maria Garcia <maria.garcia@colossuscloud.com>, sre@edgewave.com, procurement@edgewave.com

Subject: Re: Private deployment interface catalog + traffic fingerprint review — package

Maria — attaching the deliverables per your request: 1) annotated interface catalog (PDF) with control-plane vs data-plane callouts, 2) wiring diagram (drawio export) annotated with mTLS and KV-cache boundaries, and 3) a small CSV showing representative traffic fingerprints. Summary of action items and answers to your questions below: 

Action items (next steps):
- EdgeWave SRE: review the attached CSV against your firewall/NAT test vectors and flag any outliers by 2026-08-18.
- Procurement: if EdgeWave wants managed observability or license-checks enabled, note that those will be listed as optional outbound endpoints and will require explicit SLA/contract language.
- Redwood Ops: prepare a short runbook snippet for KV-cache replication if EdgeWave requests cross-region replication later.

Quick clarifications:
- Non-standard egress: telemetry.redwood.com (optional), license.redwood.com (optional), and ops-trace.redwood.com (only if tracing is enabled). All three are opt-in and we will not enable them by default in the private deployment.
- SLA: any opt-in managed services will get separate SLA addenda. Local private-plane control and inference endpoints are covered by the base Dedicated SLA.
- Diagrams: controlplane_dataplane_wire_v1.drawio (native) is shared in Drive for your engineers to pull and annotate.

Attachments: edgewave_iface_catalog_v1.pdf, controlplane_dataplane_wire_v1.drawio, traffic-fingerprint-sample.csv

Happy to jump on a short call to walk through the CSV if helpful — available tomorrow 10–11am PT.

Best — Soojin
